- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in early 30-day forecasts, especially after low points or dips; adjust upward by 2–5% for sudden upward momentum.
- Overestimates late-period price declines after spikes; apply downward correction of 3–8% for post-peak corrections.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias; increase forecasted mean by 1–3% to account for momentum.
- Forecasts lag by 2–5 days in capturing true turning points; shift forecast horizon forward by 1–2 days for better alignment with actual price shifts.
- After a sharp spike, model overcorrects downward; reduce forecasted drop by 1–3% to avoid premature reversal.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from 30-day mean, adjust forecast to align with 18-day moving average for better short-term accuracy.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), avoid overfitting to recent volatility; use 30-day median as baseline for correction.
